findings.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 — Shard path applies applyTemplateVariables (with request.filters) and then hands the already-interpolated, shard-rewritten targets to runSplitQuery (line 163, subRequest still carries `filters` via `...request` at line 154), which re-applies it at querySplitting.ts:299, so templating and ad-hoc filter injection run at least twice per sharded query.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 — The test asserts `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times (1 in runShardSplitQuery + 1 per 4 sub-requests), which locks in the redundant re-interpolation as expected behavior instead of catching it.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 — Magic `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` (1 in runShardSplitQuery + 1 per runSplitQuery sub-request) enshrines repeated interpolation of already-interpolated/sharded queries instead of asserting it is called once per target with (query, scopedVars, filters).

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 — No test passes request.filters or request.scopedVars, so ad-hoc filter forwarding is untested, as is filters getting applied twice (shard, then runSplitQuery per sub-request, then again downstream since runQuery is always mocked).

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 — Shard path applies applyTemplateVariables (with request.filters) and then hands the already-interpolated, shard-rewritten targets to runSplitQuery (line 163, subRequest still carries `filters` via `...request` at line 154), which re-applies it at querySplitting.ts:299, so templating and ad-hoc filter injection run at least twice per sharded query.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `runShardSplitQuery` now applies `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` when building `queries`, and `runSplitQuery` independently applies `applyTemplateVariables` to `request.targets`. However, the diff does not show `runShardSplitQuery` (or `splitQueriesByStreamShard`) handing those already-interpolated targets into `runSplitQuery`, nor the cited line numbers (154/163) are present here. Without seeing a call chain where sharded, interpolated targets are passed to `runSplitQuery`, the claim of “re-applies it … at least twice per sharded query” is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — Ad-hoc filters get baked into target.expr, but the sub-requests still carry `request.filters` (`{ ...request, targets }` at lines 315/337/344), so the runQuery -> DataSourceWithBackend.query path can re-apply applyTemplateVariables and inject duplicate matchers such as `{a="b", x="y", x="y"}`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes both runSplitQuery() and runShardSplitQuery() to pre-apply template variables via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`, which (per the finding) can bake ad-hoc `request.filters` into `target.expr`. The diff does not show any corresponding change to strip/clear `request.filters` when later constructing sub-requests (the finding references `{ ...request, targets }` at other lines not included here). Whether duplicate matchers actually occur depends on downstream behavior (e.g., whether `runQuery`/DataSourceWithBackend.query re-applies templates/filters), which is not verifiable from this diff alone. Still, the change clearly introduces a risk of double-applying filters because filters are now incorporated into the query objects earlier while still being carried on the request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 — The test asserts `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times (1 in runShardSplitQuery + 1 per 4 sub-requests), which locks in the redundant re-interpolation as expected behavior instead of catching it.

adjudication.rationale: In `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts`, the existing test “Interpolates queries before running” was changed to `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5);`, which hard-codes an internal call count rather than validating the externally observable behavior (e.g., that the executed queries are interpolated). From the diff, `runShardSplitQuery` itself only maps `applyTemplateVariables` once over `request.targets`, so asserting an exact total of 5 calls couples the test to additional internal re-processing elsewhere (not shown here) and makes the test brittle, effectively codifying that extra calls are acceptable/expected rather than flagging them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.test.ts:78 — The fake templateSrv.replace rewrites `$__auto` without looking at scopedVars, but the real Loki applyTemplateVariables leaves backend macros (`$__auto`/`$__interval`) for backend interpolation, so the new "Interpolates queries before execution" tests (also shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:87) only prove what the mock does.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new tests that provide a mock `replace` implementation (via `createLokiDatasource`) which replaces `$__auto` and `$step`, and new production code that calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` before executing/splitting queries. However, the finding’s core claim—"the real Loki applyTemplateVariables leaves backend macros ($__auto/$__interval) for backend interpolation"—is not verifiable from the diff because `applyTemplateVariables`’s real implementation is not shown. The observation that the tests reflect the mock behavior is true but the asserted mismatch with real behavior is speculative given only this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — On the shard path, templateSrv.replace runs a second time on already-interpolated exprs, so a variable value that itself contains `$name`/`${name}` gets expanded again, which changes the query the user wrote.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows shard-path interpolation being changed from `interpolateVariablesInQueries(...)` to a single `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` in `shardQuerySplitting.ts`, and non-shard path similarly mapping `applyTemplateVariables` in `querySplitting.ts`. Nothing in the provided diff demonstrates `templateSrv.replace` (or `applyTemplateVariables`) running a *second* time on already-interpolated expressions on the shard path; any additional interpolation would have to occur inside `splitQueriesByStreamShard(...)`/other code not shown. The finding also cites `querySplitting.ts:299` while describing the shard path, which is inconsistent with the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:300 — querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable now runs on the interpolated expr, so if `$__range` is ever resolved on the frontend (via scopedVars) the range-variable guard stops matching and range queries are silently time-split with wrong `$__range` values.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior by interpolating each target via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` before `partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` in `runSplitQuery()` (and similarly in `runShardSplitQuery()`), so any splitting-eligibility checks now see the *interpolated* `expr`. If `querySupportsSplitting` / a range-variable guard is implemented as a string check for `$__range`/similar, this ordering would indeed bypass that guard. However, the diff does not show the implementation of `querySupportsSplitting`/`isQueryWithRangeVariable` or confirm how `$__range` is resolved, so the “silently time-split with wrong `$__range` values” consequence can’t be verified from the diff alone; it’s a plausible edge-case concern tied to the changed ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:50 — The empty-expr filter now runs before interpolation instead of after, so a target whose expr is only a variable that resolves to '' is kept; the nested runSplitQuery then drops it, leaving a group with zero requests, and runSplitGroupedQueries throws at querySplitting.ts:96 (`[0].partition` of undefined) inside the groupTargetsByQueryType promise, so the panel hangs and the other shards never run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the order so that `filter((query) => query.expr)` happens before template interpolation in both `runShardSplitQuery` (now `request.targets.filter(...).map(applyTemplateVariables(...))`) and `runSplitQuery` (same pattern). That means a target whose `expr` is a non-empty template (e.g., `$var`) but interpolates to `''` would not be filtered out after interpolation. However, the finding’s specific failure chain (nested `runSplitQuery` dropping it, leading to a zero-request group and a crash at `querySplitting.ts:96`) is not verifiable from the provided diff and is partly contradicted by the new `runSplitQuery` logic (it also does not re-filter after interpolation). The actionable, diff-grounded issue is the missing post-interpolation `expr` filtering; the claimed hang/exception details can’t be confirmed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — On the shard path, targets are already interpolated by runShardSplitQuery and then interpolated again here with the same subRequest.filters (the test now expects 5 calls), so ad-hoc filters are applied twice (label filters after a parser are not deduplicated) and variable values containing `$name` text are interpolated a second time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `runSplitQuery` now interpolates targets via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)`, and `runShardSplitQuery` also interpolates its own `request.targets` the same way before calling `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. However, the diff does not show any code path where shard-splitting calls into `runSplitQuery` with already-interpolated targets, nor any evidence that ad-hoc filters are applied twice. The claim about “interpolated again here” and “ad-hoc filters are applied twice” cannot be verified from the provided hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 — Magic `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` (1 in runShardSplitQuery + 1 per runSplitQuery sub-request) enshrines repeated interpolation of already-interpolated/sharded queries instead of asserting it is called once per target with (query, scopedVars, filters).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `runShardSplitQuery` to call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` per target, and `runSplitQuery` now *also* maps `applyTemplateVariables(...)` over `request.targets` before partitioning/splitting. In `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts`, the assertion was updated from `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` to `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)`, which bakes in the current internal behavior (initial interpolation + additional interpolations during subsequent split sub-requests). This is a brittle, implementation-coupled test expectation and can normalize repeated interpolation rather than asserting the more direct contract (called once per original target with the expected arguments). The diff alone doesn’t prove this causes incorrect runtime behavior, but it’s a concrete test/design issue grounded in the changed calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:56 — applyTemplateVariables mock mutates the target in place and returns the same object, so tests still pass if the code ignores the return value or later reuses request.targets (real impl returns a new object).

adjudication.rationale: In shardQuerySplitting.test.ts the applyTemplateVariables mockImplementation mutates the passed-in LokiQuery object (e.g., `query.expr = ...`) and returns the same reference. That makes the tests less strict because they would still observe interpolated `expr`/`step` even if the implementation under test didn’t rely on the return value (since the original object would be modified). The diff shows the in-place mutation in the mocks; however, the claim about the real implementation returning a new object isn’t verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 — No test passes request.filters or request.scopedVars, so ad-hoc filter forwarding is untested, as is filters getting applied twice (shard, then runSplitQuery per sub-request, then again downstream since runQuery is always mocked).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds forwarding of `request.filters` (and `request.scopedVars`) into `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` in both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` (`.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))`). The added/updated tests shown only assert interpolation of `$__auto`/`$step` and do not explicitly exercise non-empty `request.filters` (or any ad-hoc filter behavior), so this newly introduced behavior is not directly covered by tests in the diff. However, the claim about filters being applied twice is not verifiable from this diff alone because the downstream behavior and sub-request flow aren’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — Time splitting now partitions log vs metric queries and checks splitting support on the interpolated expr, but no querySplitting test uses a variable-only expr (e.g. `$query` resolving to a metric query) to cover this behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: In `runSplitQuery` the targets are now interpolated via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` before `partition(queries, ...)` and before `isLogsQuery(query.expr)` is applied, which changes behavior when `expr` content is determined by templating (e.g., an expr that is just `$query` resolving to a metric/log query). The newly added test in `querySplitting.test.ts` only covers interpolation of `__$auto` and `$step` within an already-metric expression (`count_over_time(...)`), and does not cover the specific case where interpolation changes the query type/splitting support classification. This is a concrete missing-test gap tied to the new `.map(applyTemplateVariables...)` logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84 — New shard interpolation test would still pass if runShardSplitQuery stopped interpolating, because runSplitQuery re-interpolates each sub-request and the selector has no variables.

adjudication.rationale: The new test in `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts` (“Interpolates queries before execution”) only asserts that the *final* `datasource.runQuery` call received an interpolated `expr`/`step`, not that `runShardSplitQuery` itself performed interpolation. In this diff, `runSplitQuery()` was also changed to always call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` on targets before execution, so if shard splitting ultimately routes through `runSplitQuery` for sub-requests, interpolation could still occur even if `runShardSplitQuery` stopped interpolating. The test would then not uniquely protect the new `.map(datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` logic in `runShardSplitQuery`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.test.ts:78 — Stub `replace` rewrites `$__auto` without looking at scopedVars, so the test asserts the stub's output rather than real templateSrv behavior (real applyTemplateVariables removes __auto/__interval/__range from scopedVars for backend interpolation).

adjudication.rationale: The added test in querySplitting.test.ts intentionally stubs the datasource’s templateSrv `replace` function to verify that `runSplitQuery` calls `applyTemplateVariables` before `runQuery` and that the interpolated values are passed through (expr/step become `5m`). The diff does not show any logic about removing `__auto/__interval/__range` from `scopedVars` inside `applyTemplateVariables`, nor any backend-interpolation mechanism that the test contradicts. The complaint about not “looking at scopedVars” and asserting against stubbed output is not a verifiable defect from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.test.ts:85 — Interpolation assertions only check runQuery call[0], so only one of the three time-split chunks is verified to get interpolated targets.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `Interpolates queries before execution` in `querySplitting.test.ts`, the assertions inspect only `datasource.runQuery.mock.calls[0][0].targets[0]` (first call). Given `runSplitQuery` is designed to split a request into multiple chunked `runQuery` invocations (as indicated by other tests in the same file discussing multiple chunks/requests), this test does not verify that interpolation is applied consistently to subsequent chunk requests. This is a test coverage/completeness issue, not a production defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:298 — No test asserts that hidden or empty queries are not passed to applyTemplateVariables (the filter order before map is not covered by tests in either module).

adjudication.rationale: In both runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts) and runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts), the code now filters out hidden/empty queries before calling `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`. The newly added interpolation tests only assert the interpolated `expr`/`step` on the first executed query, and existing tests assert call counts, but none explicitly verify that queries with `hide: true` or missing/empty `expr` are *not* passed into `applyTemplateVariables`. So the finding about missing test coverage for the filter-before-map behavior is supported by the diff.
